source.original_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, let γ=stdGaussian(E) be its centered standard identity-covariance Gaussian, and let S={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Let P be a probability law on E×ℝ with first marginal γ, p a finite real polynomial, and the actual response (x,y)↦y square-integrable under P. For each parameter probability μ on S, define f_μ(x)=∫_S p(inner(w,x))dμ(w), V_μ(w)=2∫(f_μ(x)−y)p(inner(w,x))dP(x,y), g_μ(w)=gradient(V_μ)(w), and G_μ(w)=g_μ(w)−inner(g_μ(w),w)w. For w,u in S define c(w,u)=arccos(inner(w,u)); let Π(μ,ν) be all probability measures on S×S with marginals μ,ν, and Q(μ,ν)=inf_{π in Π(μ,ν)}∫c²dπ, an extended nonnegative cost. Then the integrand defining V_μ is integrable at every ambient weight and its actual ambient gradient exists there. There are positive C₁,C₂, chosen before all parameter laws and unit weights, such that G_μ(w) is tangent, norm(G_μ(w))≤C₁, Q(μ,ν) is finite, and norm(G_μ(w)−G_ν(u))≤C₂(sqrt(Q(μ,ν))+c(w,u)). No independence of response/input or derivative, domination, mean-bound, integral-identity or gradient oracle is assumed. Constants may depend on E,p,P, including the response L² norm. The theorem concerns the explicit angular cost and projected ambient gradient; it does not assert an intrinsic path-length identity, an installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API, teacher/noise construction or full model convergence.

theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : Measure (E × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (hGaussian : P.map Prod.fst = ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2) 2 P) :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let predictor : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ x => ∫ w, p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ ∂μ
    let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w =>
      2 * ∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P
    let grad : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => gradient (V μ) w
    let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => grad μ w-⟪grad μ w,w⟫_ℝ • w
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
        (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
    ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
      (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        (∀ w : E, Integrable (fun z : E × ℝ =>
            (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) P ∧
          HasGradientAt (V μ) (grad μ w) w) ∧
        ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
        Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
          ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
            C₂*((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+c (w,u))

blind_reconstruction.text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E with its Borel measurable structure, every joint probability P on E times R whose actual first-coordinate pushforward P.map Prod.fst equals stdGaussian(E), every real polynomial p, and a supplied witness MemLp(z->z.2,2,P) for the actual response coordinate, make the following definitions. Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1} with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and denote the ambient representative of w:S by w_bar. For every mu:Measure S and x:E define predictor(mu,x)=integral_S p.eval(inner_product_E(w_bar,x)) dmu(w). Define V(mu,w)=2*integral_{E times R}(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) dP(z), for every ambient w:E. Define grad(mu,w)=gradient(V(mu,.),w), the actual Mathlib full ambient gradient, and G(mu,w)=grad(mu,w)-inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),w) times w. Define c(w,u)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)) on S times S. Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over actual measures gamma whose first marginal is mu and second marginal is nu. The empty feasible infimum is infinity; no optimizer is selected or asserted. All predictor and potential integrals are actual real Bochner integrals, totalized to zero if their integrands fail to be integrable. The gradient definition is totalized at points without the corresponding Frechet derivative. Then the following full conclusion holds: There exist C1,C2:R with C1>0 and C2>0, uniform for all subsequent laws and unit weights. For every probability mu on S, and every ambient w:E, the scalar function z->(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under P, and HasGradientAt(V(mu,.),grad(mu,w),w) holds. For every such probability mu and every w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and, for all w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). The response membership supplies almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm under the true joint law; no independence or product decomposition follows from the Gaussian marginal identity. All response values in V are the actual z.2. The constants are existentially chosen once, before every measure and unit-point quantifier, and may depend on the fixed E,P,p and its response moment data but not on mu,nu,w,u. The explicit integrability conclusion concerns the displayed cross term under P for every ambient w, not merely for unit or supported weights. The gradient assertion is a genuine full ambient Frechet differentiability conclusion, with derivative v->inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),v); it is not merely the use of a totalized gradient symbol. Mu is fixed when taking this derivative. The statement does not supply a further closed formula for grad involving a derivative polynomial or an adjoint operator. For a unit ambient point w, the definition of G is the orthogonal projection of the full ambient gradient onto w-perpendicular; for nonunit w it is only the stated algebraic subtraction. The norm and law-plus-angle comparison are asserted only at exact unit points of S and concern G, not an unrestricted bound on grad. The parameter probabilities may be arbitrary, including nonatomic laws. Definitions exist for arbitrary measures, while the analytic and transport-finiteness claims have the displayed probability premises. Finiteness of Q makes its extended square root finite and toReal its ordinary nonnegative real value, rather than its convention zero at infinity. Q=0 is allowed. No new metric or geodesic structure, chosen optimal coupling, differentiability in the law variable, positive-dimensionality assumption, or nonzero-polynomial assumption is asserted. If S is empty, the probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous but positive C1,C2 are still required to exist.

theorem gaussian_polynomial_joint_potential_projected_gradient_transport_control
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : Measure (E × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (hGaussian : P.map Prod.fst = ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2) 2 P) :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let predictor : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ x => ∫ w, p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ ∂μ
    let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w =>
      2 * ∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P
    let grad : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => gradient (V μ) w
    let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => grad μ w-⟪grad μ w,w⟫_ℝ • w
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
        (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
    ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
      (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        (∀ w : E, Integrable (fun z : E × ℝ =>
            (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) P ∧
          HasGradientAt (V μ) (grad μ w) w) ∧
        ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
        Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
          ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
            C₂*((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+c (w,u)) := by
  classical
  let : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  dsimp only
  let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
  let predictor : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ x => ∫ w, p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ ∂μ
  let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w =>
    2 * ∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P
  let grad : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => gradient (V μ) w
  let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w => grad μ w-⟪grad μ w,w⟫_ℝ • w
  let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
  let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
      (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
  change ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
      (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        (∀ w : E, Integrable (fun z : E × ℝ =>
            (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) P ∧
          HasGradientAt (V μ) (grad μ w) w) ∧
        ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
        Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
          ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
            C₂*((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+c (w,u))
  obtain ⟨hf,hdf,D,hD,hDiff,M₁,M₂,hM₁,hM₂,hBound,hLip⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialDifferentiation.actual_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_derivative_bounds (E := E) p
  have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : E × ℝ → E) P (stdGaussian E) :=
    ⟨measurable_fst,hGaussian⟩
  let J : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P :=
    Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.fst hmarg
  let T : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := J.toContinuousLinearMap
  let hfP : ∀ w : E, MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) 2 P :=
    fun w => (hf w).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  let F : E → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => (hfP w).toLp (fun z => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ)
  let DP : E → E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => T.comp (D w)
  have hFeq (w : E) : F w = T ((hf w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ)) := rfl
  have hFP (w : E) : HasFDerivAt F (DP w) w := by
    have he : F = fun u => T ((hf u).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ)) := funext hFeq
    rw [he]
    exact T.hasFDerivAt.comp w (hDiff w)
  have hPB (w : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) : ‖DP w‖ ≤ M₁ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ hM₁.le
    intro v
    change ‖J (D w v)‖ ≤ M₁*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w).le_opNorm v).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hBound w hw) (norm_nonneg v))
  have hPL (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖DP w-DP u‖ ≤ M₂*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (mul_nonneg hM₂.le (norm_nonneg _))
    intro v
    change ‖T (D w v)-T (D u v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [← map_sub]
    change ‖J ((D w-D u) v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w-D u).le_opNorm v).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hLip u w hu hw) (norm_nonneg v))
  let label : Lp ℝ 2 P := hlabel.toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2)
  let K : S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => F w.1
  let mean : Measure S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun μ => ∫ w, K w ∂μ
  obtain ⟨C₁,C₂,hC₁,hC₂,hpoint,hlaw⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureLawGradient.quadratic_feature_law_gradient_angular_transport_control
      F DP hFP M₁ M₂ hM₁.le hM₂.le hPB hPL label
  obtain ⟨hfS,hcont,havg⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialAveraging.gaussian_polynomial_parameter_average_L2 (E := E) p
  have hMeanClass (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      ∃ hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P,
        hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = mean μ := by
    obtain ⟨hscalar,hint,hmean,hident⟩ := havg μ hμ
    let hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P :=
      hmean.comp_measurePreserving hmarg
    refine ⟨hpred,?_⟩
    calc
      hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = T (hmean.toLp (predictor μ)) := rfl
      _ = T (∫ w, (hfS w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ) ∂μ) := congrArg T hident
      _ = mean μ := (T.integral_comp_comm hint).symm
  have hMeanAE (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => mean μ z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) := by
    obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
    rw [← hident]
    exact hpred.coeFn_toLp
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => (mean μ-label) z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1-z.2) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_sub (mean μ) label,hMeanAE μ hμ,hlabel.coeFn_toLp]
      with z hs hm hy
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hs
    rw [hs,hm,hy]
  have hPot (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      V μ = fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ-label,F w⟫_ℝ := by
    funext w
    change 2 * (∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P) = _
    rw [L2.inner_def]
    congr 1
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hResidual μ hμ,(hfP w).coeFn_toLp] with z hr hw
    change F w z = p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ at hw
    simp only [Real.inner_apply,hr,hw]
  have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) w := by
    rw [hPot μ hμ]
    exact (hpoint μ hμ).2.1 w
  have hG (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      G μ w = (2 : ℝ) • ((DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label) -
        ⟪(DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label),w⟫_ℝ • w) := by
    dsimp only [G,grad]
    rw [(hGrad μ hμ w).gradient]
    simp only [smul_sub,real_inner_smul_left,smul_smul]
  refine ⟨C₁,C₂,hC₁,hC₂,?_,?_⟩
  · intro μ hμ
    refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
    · intro w
      obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
      refine ⟨(hpred.sub hlabel).integrable_mul (hfP w),?_⟩
      change HasGradientAt (V μ) (gradient (V μ) w) w
      rw [(hGrad μ hμ w).gradient]
      exact hGrad μ hμ w
    · intro w
      rw [hG μ hμ w.1]
      exact (hpoint μ hμ).2.2 w
  · intro μ ν hμ hν
    refine ⟨(hlaw μ ν hμ hν).1,?_⟩
    intro w u
    rw [hG μ hμ w.1,hG ν hν u.1]
    exact (hlaw μ ν hμ hν).2 w u

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialGradient

steps.title: Differentiate the Gaussian feature in L2
steps.text: Start with \(\Phi(w)(x)=p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) in \(H_0=L^2(\gamma)\). The existing Gaussian derivative theorem constructs its actual Fréchet derivative \(D_0(w)\), a uniform operator bound and an operator Lipschitz bound on the closed unit ball. No feature or derivative witness is an input.
steps.detail: Literal whole-module excerpt. Local definitions and earlier derived facts are available in the optional complete theorem; no extra public hypotheses are introduced.

steps.title: Pull the feature into the joint data space
steps.text: The input-marginal identity makes the first-coordinate projection measure preserving. Composition defines a linear isometry \(J:H_0\to H=L^2(P)\), even when response and input are dependent. Set \(F(w)=J\Phi(w)\) and \(D_P(w)=J\circ D_0(w)\). The isometry preserves both operator estimates.
steps.lean:
have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : E × ℝ → E) P (stdGaussian E) :=
    ⟨measurable_fst,hGaussian⟩
  let J : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P :=
    Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.fst hmarg
  let T : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := J.toContinuousLinearMap
  let hfP : ∀ w : E, MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) 2 P :=
    fun w => (hf w).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  let F : E → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => (hfP w).toLp (fun z => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ)
  let DP : E → E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => T.comp (D w)
  have hFeq (w : E) : F w = T ((hf w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ)) := rfl
  have hFP (w : E) : HasFDerivAt F (DP w) w := by
    have he : F = fun u => T ((hf u).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ)) := funext hFeq
    rw [he]
    exact T.hasFDerivAt.comp w (hDiff w)
  have hPB (w : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) : ‖DP w‖ ≤ M₁ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ hM₁.le
    intro v
    change ‖J (D w v)‖ ≤ M₁*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w).le_opNorm v).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hBound w hw) (norm_nonneg v))
  have hPL (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖DP w-DP u‖ ≤ M₂*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (mul_nonneg hM₂.le (norm_nonneg _))
    intro v
    change ‖T (D w v)-T (D u v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [← map_sub]
    change ‖J ((D w-D u) v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w-D u).le_opNorm v).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hLip u w hu hw) (norm_nonneg v))

steps.title: Identify the true parameter average
steps.text: Let \(\ell(x,y)=y\) in \(H\) and \(m_\mu=\int F(w)\,d\mu(w)\), a Bochner integral. The existing Gaussian averaging theorem puts the literal predictor in \(L^2(\gamma)\) and identifies its class with the feature mean. Pull back this identity and commute \(J\) with the Bochner integral. Thus \(m_\mu\) is the \(L^2(P)\) class of the predictor, and \(m_\mu-\ell\) represents the residual almost everywhere.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨hfS,hcont,havg⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialAveraging.gaussian_polynomial_parameter_average_L2 (E := E) p
  have hMeanClass (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      ∃ hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P,
        hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = mean μ := by
    obtain ⟨hscalar,hint,hmean,hident⟩ := havg μ hμ
    let hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P :=
      hmean.comp_measurePreserving hmarg
    refine ⟨hpred,?_⟩
    calc
      hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = T (hmean.toLp (predictor μ)) := rfl
      _ = T (∫ w, (hfS w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ) ∂μ) := congrArg T hident
      _ = mean μ := (T.integral_comp_comm hint).symm
  have hMeanAE (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => mean μ z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) := by
    obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
    rw [← hident]
    exact hpred.coeFn_toLp
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => (mean μ-label) z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1-z.2) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_sub (mean μ) label,hMeanAE μ hμ,hlabel.coeFn_toLp]
      with z hs hm hy
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hs
    rw [hs,hm,hy]

steps.title: Recover the literal scalar potential
steps.text: The residual and every ambient feature belong to \(L^2(P)\), so their product is integrable. The inner product and the almost-everywhere identities identify the literal potential with the displayed ambient function. This function identity is proved inside the theorem.
steps.lean:
have hPot (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      V μ = fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ-label,F w⟫_ℝ := by
    funext w
    change 2 * (∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P) = _
    rw [L2.inner_def]
    congr 1
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hResidual μ hμ,(hfP w).coeFn_toLp] with z hr hw
    change F w z = p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ at hw
    simp only [Real.inner_apply,hr,hw]

steps.title: Differentiate and identify the actual gradient
steps.text: Apply the existing quadratic feature-law theorem to \(F,D_P,\ell\) with the bounds just proved. Transport its ambient derivative across the function identity. Uniqueness identifies the displayed vector with the actual ambient gradient of the literal potential at every ambient weight.
steps.lean:
have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) w := by
    rw [hPot μ hμ]
    exact (hpoint μ hμ).2.1 w

steps.title: Project onto tangent directions
steps.text: For a unit weight, let \(P_wz=z-\langle z,w\rangle w\) and \(G_\mu(w)=P_w\nabla V_\mu(w)\). Substituting the gradient identity lets the feature-law theorem supply tangency and a positive uniform norm constant \(C_1\).
steps.lean:
have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) w := by
    rw [hPot μ hμ]
    exact (hpoint μ hμ).2.1 w
  have hG (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      G μ w = (2 : ℝ) • ((DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label) -
        ⟪(DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label),w⟫_ℝ • w) := by
    dsimp only [G,grad]
    rw [(hGrad μ hμ w).gradient]
    simp only [smul_sub,real_inner_smul_left,smul_smul]
steps.detail: Literal whole-module excerpt. Local definitions and earlier derived facts are available in the optional complete theorem; no extra public hypotheses are introduced.

steps.title: Keep the angular cost and pass to joint law/point control
steps.text: Use \(c(w,u)=\arccos\langle w,u\rangle\) on \(S\), and take the infimum of \(\int c^2\,d\pi\) over all couplings. The feature-law parent proves finiteness of \(Q\) and the projected Hilbert-space estimate. Substitute the actual-gradient identity for both laws. The constants \(C_1,C_2\) precede every law and weight quantifier; they may depend on \(E,p,P\), including the response norm.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨C₁,C₂,hC₁,hC₂,?_,?_⟩
  · intro μ hμ
    refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
    · intro w
      obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
      refine ⟨(hpred.sub hlabel).integrable_mul (hfP w),?_⟩
      change HasGradientAt (V μ) (gradient (V μ) w) w
      rw [(hGrad μ hμ w).gradient]
      exact hGrad μ hμ w
    · intro w
      rw [hG μ hμ w.1]
      exact (hpoint μ hμ).2.2 w
  · intro μ ν hμ hν
    refine ⟨(hlaw μ ν hμ hν).1,?_⟩
    intro w u
    rw [hG μ hμ w.1,hG ν hν u.1]
    exact (hlaw μ ν hμ hν).2 w u

lesson.lean_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, let γ=stdGaussian(E) be its centered standard identity-covariance Gaussian, and let S={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Let P be a probability law on E×ℝ with first marginal γ, p a finite real polynomial, and the actual response (x,y)↦y square-integrable under P. For each parameter probability μ on S, define f_μ(x)=∫_S p(inner(w,x))dμ(w), V_μ(w)=2∫(f_μ(x)−y)p(inner(w,x))dP(x,y), g_μ(w)=gradient(V_μ)(w), and G_μ(w)=g_μ(w)−inner(g_μ(w),w)w. For w,u in S define c(w,u)=arccos(inner(w,u)); let Π(μ,ν) be all probability measures on S×S with marginals μ,ν, and Q(μ,ν)=inf_{π in Π(μ,ν)}∫c²dπ, an extended nonnegative cost. Then the integrand defining V_μ is integrable at every ambient weight and its actual ambient gradient exists there. There are positive C₁,C₂, chosen before all parameter laws and unit weights, such that G_μ(w) is tangent, norm(G_μ(w))≤C₁, Q(μ,ν) is finite, and norm(G_μ(w)−G_ν(u))≤C₂(sqrt(Q(μ,ν))+c(w,u)). No independence of response/input or derivative, domination, mean-bound, integral-identity or gradient oracle is assumed. Constants may depend on E,p,P, including the response L² norm. The theorem concerns the explicit angular cost and projected ambient gradient; it does not assert an intrinsic path-length identity, an installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API, teacher/noise construction or full model convergence.
